A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAC-B research, with readable main text, equations, tables, and complete appendices. The material can be matched despite reformatting, appendix renumbering, and the added checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical regret and convergence bounds with proofs. Tables 1–2 compare analytical guarantees; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, with no experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Its checklist explicitly confirms the absence of experiments.

M1.justification: NAC-B retains the same batched critic and natural-gradient updates, linear critic, and policy update. Section 3 incorporates and expands explanations from v1 Appendix B without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. The analyzed average-reward unichain setting is retained; neural critics and broader MDP classes are discussed only as future directions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparison algorithms and analytical guarantees. No experimentally evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an experimental evaluation protocol. The theoretical batch sizes, iteration schedules, and single-trajectory construction remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The biased-random-walk example added in Remark 2 is a cited theoretical illustration, not a newly conducted test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained theoretical bias, variance, and probability bounds are not new empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries appear in either version. The regret and sample-complexity comparisons in Tables 1–2 and the principal convergence bounds retain their values.

T1.justification: The Lemma 2 proof changes transient-state counting from min(t, T_theta) to min(t, T_theta - 1) and adjusts the summation boundaries around the hitting time (v1 Appendix D.1; v2 Appendix C.1). Section 3 expands the critic approximation derivation, and Remark 2 adds a mixing-time inequality. The main theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: order-optimal square-root regret under unichain assumptions, general policy parameterization, function approximation, batching, and online operation without simulator access.

C2.justification: v2 substantially replaces the closing qualifications: v1 Appendix I discusses dimension dependence and the unresolved justification of objective smoothness, whereas v2 Remarks 2–3 discuss exploration constants, comparison with mixing times, and conjectural extensions beyond unichain policies. Smoothness remains required by Theorem 1, but its detailed caveat disappears.

D1.justification: Section 3 explicitly identifies the final natural-gradient inner iterate as the estimate used for the policy update. This clarifies the algorithm's readout; the learning-rate prescriptions and trajectory budget remain unchanged, and no code, data, or implementation resources are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on constrained policy gradients, constrained actor–critic methods, neural critics, and Markov-chain mixing. It removes the Kumar et al. smoothness-related reference and AdaNav alongside the deleted discussion. Remark 2 adds positioning against ergodic actor–critic guarantees; the principal novelty claim is retained.

P1.justification: Section 3 integrates and expands the former update-rule appendix, introduces clearer subroutine labels, and removes that standalone appendix. v2 also revises closing remarks, updates author information, and inserts a NeurIPS checklist. Most scientific prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS typography, margins, and title formatting, reflowing equations, tables, and the algorithm box. Both comparison tables retain their structure and content, and neither version contains research figures.

improvement.justification: v2 improves access to the method explanation and revises proof indices, but removes v1's substantive discussion of the unresolved smoothness assumption. New Remark 2 also asserts C <= 7 t_mix without deriving the connection to the hitting-time constant defined in Section 2. These clarity gains and unresolved theoretical qualifications prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
